_meta.title: Erratum 1 to the frozen eclipse predictions (2026-08-12): our own errors
_meta.author: funwithscience.net dome-model-review (operator-approved)
_meta.immutability_note: The frozen file is unchanged and its claims stand as registered. This addendum records errors in OUR pre-registered claims. It is a separate dated file, as the frozen file's immutability_notice requires.

summary: Two of our standard-physics claims were not what they said they were. B1-G-005 (the Hartland partial-eclipse depth) was labelled as a NASA local-circumstances calculation but was never computed. The number came from our own review prose, and it is wrong by 6.4 percentage points, three times the stated tolerance. B1-M-001 (the magnetic amplitude) cites a paper under the wrong authors and title, and its range was adapted from literature rather than computed for this eclipse. These are our errors. They are not failures of the heliocentric/standard model: correctly computed, the standard ephemeris gives exactly what was observed at Hartland. The geometric claims that discriminate between the models (B1-G-001 path width, B1-G-002 duration) were right, and the geometric verdict against the dome is unaffected.

attribution_rule.rule: A failed prediction is attributed to a MODEL only when the predicted value follows from that model's stated mechanism and parameters, as its proponent specified them. A value that misstates, mis-cites or loosely approximates a model is attributed to whoever wrote it down (failure_attribution = 'analyst_representation').
attribution_rule.applies_to: Both sides equally. The dome's pre-registered magnetic claims (PRED-095, PRED-TIER-1) are held to the same test. See symmetry_obligation.

registered.review_prose: partial coverage lasts roughly 2 h 45 min (data/sections.json §4.2.7, cited by the frozen file)
registered.stated_source: NASA SE2026Aug12T Besselian elements + local-circumstances calculation for Hartland coordinates

independent_checks: timeanddate.com, Bideford (~20 km E), fetched 2026-09-27: magnitude 0.947, 17:17-19:08 UT. The same script at Bideford gives 0.947 and 17:17:42-19:08:31 UT.

entries.error: Obscuration is 6.4 pp low (3.2 times the ±2 pp tolerance). The prose duration is 54 min too long.
entries.root_cause: We found no computation record for 88 % or 2 h 45 min anywhere in the repository. The frozen-file procedure (analyst Mode 5) required each number to trace back to our own live review text. It did not require the number to trace back to a calculation. So a figure that had never been computed in the review prose was carried into an OTS-anchored claim, and it arrived with a NASA attribution it had never earned. The step that went wrong is the provenance, not the physics.
entries.bearing_on_model_comparison: None against standard physics: the standard ephemeris, correctly applied, predicts the observed circumstances. B1-G-005 was never one of the dome-discriminating claims. The partial-eclipse argument on the eclipse page does not depend on its exact value, because ~94 % coverage at Hartland strengthens it.

entries.registered_citation: Kim, V. P., & Chang, H. Y. (2018). Geomagnetic effects of solar eclipses studied with a 39-eclipse 1991-2016 INTERMAGNET ensemble. Adv. Space Res. 61: 2040-2049.
entries.correct_citation: Kim, J.-H., & Chang, H.-Y. (2018). Statistical analysis of geomagnetic field variations during solar eclipses. Advances in Space Research 61(8): 2040-2049. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asr.2018.01.022
entries.unverified_attributions: The abstract describes about 207 data sets from 100 INTERMAGNET observatories over 1991-2016 and does not state an eclipse count. The '39-eclipse' figure, and the component pattern we attributed to the paper, are unverified pending a full-text check (ISS-3101). EXP-684 already removes them from WIN-010. WIN-025 and WIN-068 wait on the full-text check.

entries.issue: The amplitude range was not computed for this eclipse
entries.registered: -25 to -5 nT signed peak at high-coverage stations under Kp < 2, tracking the shadow over 60-180 min
entries.what_was_wrong: The range was adapted from ensemble literature (partly the mis-cited paper in E-2) and from a general Sq review. It was not computed for this eclipse's geometry and local time; the frozen caveat says so. Maximum eclipse over the stations came in the late afternoon to near sunset (Sun altitude about 3-14 deg at the dome-cited stations), when the daytime ionospheric (Sq) current that an eclipse perturbs is well past its near-noon peak. We did not account for that. A range derived that way was not a faithful statement of what standard physics predicts for this event.
entries.design_defect: Under the pre-registered protocol metric, B1-M-001's band is met on ordinary non-eclipse days (at least half the high-obscuration stations are in range on 17 of 30 control days). As registered, our own claim had little power to discriminate, the same defect we found in the dome-side criterion OBS-D-02.
entries.what_this_erratum_does_not_do: It does not assign B1-M-001 a verdict. The magnetic evaluation is still in its review loop (EXP-687, curmudgeon cycle 3 pending); the verdict label, and the symmetric-labelling decision for both sides, belong in the OTS-anchored RESULTS file. The erratum fixes the attribution in advance: if the RESULTS file scores B1-M-001 as failed, the failure is ours (analyst_representation), not the standard model's. We make no claim here that a proper Sq-model run would have predicted the observed near-null; any such run would be post hoc and must be marked preregistered:false.

symmetry_obligation: Under the same rule, the dome's magnetic failure counts as a MODEL failure only if the test covers what the dome's mechanism actually computes. Our frozen file already records that the dome's own formula, at its own published coverages, gives about -10 to -13 nT at its >80 %-coverage stations (-5.0 to -12.8 nT across all nine, BOU baseline; the dome's alternate W004 baseline gives -10 to -26 nT), not the -17 to -21 nT stated in PRED-095. The RESULTS file must therefore show power against the formula-derived per-station amplitudes as well as the PRED-095 range before attributing the failure to the model rather than to the dome author's representation of it.
unchanged: B1-G-001 (294 km path width) and B1-G-002 (138.2 s) remain CONFIRMED.
PRED-ECLIPSE-2026-GEOMETRY remains FALSIFIED (the dome forces a ~1.317 km umbra).
PRED-095, PRED-TIER-1, PRED-TIER-3 and PRED-R005 remain our_verdict: pending.
process_changes: Analyst Mode 5 (monitor/prompts/analyst.md): each numeric claim now carries provenance_type 'computed' (with script path + output hash) or 'cited' (with the page/table/equation actually checked). Tracing a number to our own prose is no longer sufficient.
Curmudgeon (monitor/prompts/curmudgeon.md): a frozen-prediction review must independently recompute our own side's numeric claims before a freeze is approved, not just attack the dome side.
